title: ANTICIPATE – Understanding the influence of psychosocial factors on treatment side effects and outcomes in patients with soft tissue sarcoma
summary: Soft tissue sarcomas are a heterogeneous group of malignant tumors originating from the mesenchymal cell line. They account for less than 1% of malignant tumor diseases, which is why treatment is mostly performed at highly specialized centers. Soft tissue sarcomas at high risk of recurrence are treated at our center as part of a multimodal therapy including thermochemotherapy, radiation and surgical resection with an approximate total duration of 7-8 months. In any treatment aimed at achieving a positive effect, potential undesirable side effects must always be taken into account. Despite appropriate supportive therapy, they represent a clinically relevant problem in the care of people with cancer. In addition to direct, chemical drug components, non-specific, individual factors also appear to be responsible for the type and extent of potential side effects. In particular, the individual expectations of the patients, including their individual previous experiences, are considered to be a promising influencing factor in this respect. In the present project, about 50 patients with soft tissue sarcoma will be assessed during multimodal therapy in our center by means of three established questionnaires (B-IPQ, GEEE and QLQ-C30) regarding their expectations, subjective side effects and quality of life and a possible correlation with objectifiable toxicity, therapy response and survival. The aim of this study is to enable patient stratification by the obtained results, to better understand the interplay between psychological effects and side effects and finally to improve the treatment of our sarcoma patients. Thus, future high-risk patients could be referred earlier to supportive services, e.g. in the context of a psycho-oncological consultation.
